Element.attribute: Define technology cutover and deployment approach

Development and execution of a realistic cutover and deployment approach is a critical activity to confirm that the enhanced capabilities, processes and tools are established successfully. The approach will drive realization of benefits, enable the program to maintain an appropriate level of visibility and momentum, and determine the level of risk inherent in the upcoming transition.

When building the approach, it is important to:

  • Align the approach to all components of the organization’s operating model to clarify when changes will be implemented and determine how changes made later in the timeline can be rolled out to business units or countries that have already been transitioned.
  • Draw on the expertise within the business and technology teams to validate the feasibility of the transition approach and the subsequent detailed transition plan.
  • Manage the program as an integrated set of projects, in order to better manage dependencies.
  • Consider all stakeholders and outline how each will be engaged in transition activities throughout the project.
  • Fully train stakeholders in transition activities overall and individually-assigned area of responsibility.
  • Have business and IT managers fully engaged with stakeholders throughout the transition period.
  • Include a high level communications plan that outlines the appropriate communication mechanisms and messaging levels for each target audience.
  • Focus on the areas where overruns or higher costs can occur, such as systems and interface development, scope change, recruitment, site set-up, level of clean-up needed and knowledge transfer.

The cutover and deployment approach provides a high-level overview of changes that will result from introduction of a new solution and how the organization will manage through the transition to new capabilities, processes and tools. To assemble the approach, describe the resulting changes, and how the changes will affect roles and responsibilities within the IT organization. Present possible options for conducting the transition, outline a high-level timeline, and include an overview of cutover and deployment governance structure and processes.

To define the technology approach, consider both functional and non-functional aspects of the cutover and deployment. (The organization’s approach for business and organization transition aspects are captured and documented in a separate section of the approach document. The two sections work in tandem and are the basis for a more detailed cutover and deployment plan.)

As technology enables the business capability enhancements, the technology approach builds on the preparations made by the business, and outlines the preparations for managing the application, data and infrastructure aspects of the cutover and deployment. The approach serves as the basis for a subsequent detailed cutover and deployment plan, and includes:

  • Business cutover and deployment team touchpoints and contacts, to enable communication and teamwork
  • Technology cutover and deployment team, organization and governance
  • Technology cutover and deployment roles and responsibilities
  • Tools and repositories
  • Technology environments, locations and facilities
  • Technology processes and controls
  • Technology metrics and success criteria
  • Technology transition schedule
  • Technology failover considerations
  • Technology contingency considerations
  • Scheduling of initial post-transition technology-related processes
  • Deployment and post-go-live support, to confirm plans for cutover and future business continuity

These additional technology concerns should also be considered when drafting the approach:

  • How realization of benefits from the new capability and technology will be measured
  • Command centers as the central transition collection and distribution point
  • Replacement of legacy systems
  • Knowledge management considerations
